newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Treasury to present economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Treasury to present economic reforms.

text.p: Israel's Treasury will present the government on Sunday with a series of economic reforms aimed at liberalising foreign currency exchange and lifting state monopolies, a newspaper said on Thursday.

Treasury officials refused to comment ahead of a press briefing scheduled for Thursday afternoon but many of the measures listed in the report have been long promised by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
They include allowing Israelis to open dollar accounts in Israel and increasing the freedom of mutual and provident funds to invest abroad.
The Treasury will ask Netanyahu's cabinet to approve about 100 reforms to allow competition in public transport, local phone dialing, air travel and pharmeceuticals, according to the report.
Large government-owned companies such as Israel Electric Corp will undergo restructuring as a stage on the road to privatisation.

Privatisation and economic liberalisation were cornerstones of Netanyahu's election campaign 14 months ago. Since then, he has sold off stakes in several government-owned companies, putting him on a collision course with union leaders.

Around 60,000 workers walked off their jobs last month to protest the sale of a 12.5-percent stake in government-run Bezeq Israel Telecomm. The nation-wide strike followed weeks of sanctions by Bezeq phone workers.
Also on Sunday, the parliamentary Finance Committee was scheduled to vote on the government's approved 800 million shekel cut in the 1997 budget.
